question: Which remaining Android capability, if any, should OpenClaw accept in core first: explicit device-control commands, ADB-style access, or dynamic Android code execution?
rationale: The remaining requested capabilities expand phone control, sensitive data access, and possible arbitrary execution, so automation cannot choose the product/security boundary safely.

options.title: Approve narrow device-control commands first
options.body: Limit the next step to explicit Android brightness, volume, vibration, or find-my-phone style commands with Android permission UX, gateway allowlist policy, and focused proof.

options.title: Route high-power execution elsewhere
options.body: Keep ADB and dynamic execution out of Android core until a node-host, plugin, or approved execution API can provide explicit sandbox and approval semantics.

options.title: Defer all remaining Android control work
options.body: Leave the umbrella open as design discussion only until a maintainer-owned Android security design exists.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow device-control commands first
recommendation.body: Limit the next step to explicit Android brightness, volume, vibration, or find-my-phone style commands with Android permission UX, gateway allowlist policy, and focused proof.
